text:
Kim Park: Quick thread — seeing a weird pattern where premium tenants in eu-west are getting unexpected model-variant fallbacks to quantized variants. Dumping an example header/debug payload from one of the failing requests:

```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer ***REDACTED***
x-rw-tenant: tenant-acme
x-rw-region-prefer: eu
x-rw-tier: premium
x-rw-routing: region=eu-west;policy=smart-tier-2026-03;target=model-family-X
x-rw-decision-id: dec_20260315_9f12
x-rw-fallback: quantized-int8-v2
```

Maria Gomez: Is this from the new smart-tier policy we rolled yesterday? @sanjay

Sanjay Rao: It shouldn't be — that rollout was scoped to us-east only. @kim, can you paste the routing headers we log (the ones from the runtime)? Also: is this triggering latency or quality alerts?

Kim Park: Pasted the runtime decision blob from the trace (sanitized):

```
{
  "decision_id": "dec_20260315_9f12",
  "tenant": "tenant-acme",
  "inputs": {"tier":"premium","region_pref":"eu","request_size":512},
  "policy_version": "smart-tier-2026-03-01",
  "decision_path": ["region_check","capacity_check","cost_score"],
  "chosen_variant": "int8-v2",
  "fallback_reason": "capacity_constraint:primary-replica-full"
}
```

Frank Liu: That fallback_reason screams capacity-based fallback. Our smart router prefers keeping latency low but if the local replicas are saturated it selects a cheaper quantized variant. For premium tenants we should bias towards maintaining quality (avoid quantized) unless absolutely necessary.

Maria Gomez: We're seeing a couple of QA alerts where output quality drops. We need better visibility in the console traces: decision_reason, policy_version, score that led to fallback, and replica_id. Right now the trace is too terse to triage quickly.

Kim Park: Agreed. Proposal: console request inspector should show a lightweight "routing decision panel" with the following fields visible: inputs (tenant_tier, region_pref, model_preferences), computed scores (latency_score, cost_score, quality_risk), policy_version, fallback_chain (primary -> secondary -> fallback_variant), and raw routing headers for each hop. Mock idea below.

Sanjay Rao: Telemetry-wise I recommend we emit: decision_path (array), decision_metrics (latency_est_ms, cost_est_usd_per_k, quality_delta_pct), policy_version, replica_id, and a boolean fallback_applied. Also sample 100% of premium requests for the first 24h after any policy change and 1% otherwise.

Maria Gomez: Important: do NOT log full API keys — only token hash. Also add a quick link from the decision panel to the rollout that owns policy_version so support can ask for rollback.

Frank Liu: I'll add a small header probe in the edge proxy so we can capture `x-rw-routing`, `x-rw-decision-id`, `x-rw-policy-version`, and `x-rw-fallback` into our edge logs. Lightweight emitter, no payload duplication. Plan: push canary to eu-west (10%) today, full roll to 100% when we verify privacy and perf.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: edge-proxy: add header-probe v1 -> canary to eu-west (10%)

Kim Park: Also UX ask: in the panel show an "expected quality delta" for each fallback step with a tooltip explaining how it's computed and a link to run a quick eval on a stored prompt set. Helps support decide whether to roll back.

Sanjay Rao: And surface a rollout metric: `fallback_rate_by_tier_and_region` — canary must expose this so rollouts don't silently increase premium fallback rate. Add alert if >0.5% sustained for 1h.

Maria Gomez: :thumbsup: Can we get a small dashboard tile for "premium fallback rate by region" and an on-call alert?

Frank Liu: I'll add the metrics + Grafana panel and wire the alert rule. Will also include label convention `tenant_tier`, `region`, `policy_version`, `decision_id` for tracing. Ping me if you want specific label names.

Kim Park: Thanks all — after the canary I'll gather a couple of sample traces to attach to the incident ticket so support can replicate.

deploy-bot: canary: edge-proxy header-probe v1 -> eu-west 10% live

Maria Gomez: I'll follow up with a short runbook for support: how to read the routing decision panel and what to check first (replica_id capacity, policy_version, fallback_rate).
